title: Rigging, Raw Stock, and Opening Moves

sets.relationshipLabel: two counterparts of the same kind, paired together in either order
sets.explanation: A float and sinker, or port and starboard, are matched counterparts that only make sense as a pair — neither word leads, so either order is correct.
Hemp and flax are raw fibers spun into rope and twine, the cordage each is worked into.

sets.relationshipLabel: the drawn or cut template and the built thing it produces
sets.explanation: A pattern is cut into a sail just as a blueprint is built into a hull — the template made into the object.

sets.relationshipLabel: stage that opens the larger span
sets.explanation: A patch opens a season the way a launch opens a voyage — the first stage of a longer stretch.
